Mesillat Yesharim 11:134: And concerning all of them it is said (Proverbs 16:5): "an abomination to the Lord is every haughty heart"; and from all of them, whoever wishes to attain the trait of cleanliness must become clean, and must know and understand that pride is nothing but actual blindness, whereby a person's reason does not see his own deficiencies or recognize his own lowliness,
Mesillat Yesharim 11:135: for if he could see and recognize the truth, he would turn away and distance himself greatly from all these evil and corrupt ways. And we will speak more of this, with the help of Heaven, when we come to the trait of humility, which, because of the great difficulty in attaining it, was placed by Rabbi Pinchas among the later ones in his statement.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:136: Let us now speak of anger. There is the hot-tempered man of whom they said: whoever becomes angry is as though he worshiped idols (Zohar, Bereishit) — this is one who becomes angry at everything done against his will, and is filled with wrath until his heart is no longer with him and his judgment becomes foolish.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:137: Such a man is capable of destroying an entire world if it were within his power, for reason has no rule over him at all, and he has actually lost his senses like all the beasts of prey; and of him it is said (Job 18:4): "He tears himself apart in his anger — shall the earth be forsaken for your sake?" And he can easily fall into any kind of transgression in the world if his wrath brings him to it, for he now has no other restraint besides his own anger, and wherever it takes him, he will go.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:138: And there is another kind of hot-tempered man, further from this, who does not blaze in anger over every matter, small or great, that goes against his will; but when he does reach the point of being provoked, he becomes angry and enraged greatly — and this is the kind whom the Sages, of blessed memory, called (Avot 5:14) "hard to anger and hard to appease." And this too is certainly bad, for great damage can result from his hand in the time of his anger, and afterward he will not be able to rectify what he has twisted.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:139: And there is a milder kind of hot-tempered man, who does not become angry easily, and even when he does become angry, his anger is small, and he does not depart from the ways of reason; but he still holds on to his wrath. And this is further from harm than the previous kinds we mentioned, but even this one has certainly not attained cleanliness, for he is not even watchful yet — for as long as anger has any impression upon him, he has not left the category of the hot-tempered man.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:140: And there is one milder still: hard to anger, and his anger neither destroys nor consumes, but is only a small anger. And how long does his indignation last? A moment, and no more — that is, from the moment his anger is naturally aroused within him until his reason, too, is aroused against it. This is what the Sages, of blessed memory, said (ibid.): "hard to anger and easy to appease" — this is certainly a good portion, for a person's nature is aroused to anger, but if he overcomes it so that even at the very time of his anger it does not blaze up much, and he masters it so that even that mild anger does not remain in him for long, but passes and goes away — this is certainly praiseworthy.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:141: And they said, of blessed memory (Chullin 89a): "He hangs the earth upon nothing" (Job 26:7) — the world exists only for the sake of one who restrains his mouth at the time of strife — that is, one whose nature has already been aroused to anger, but who, in mastering himself, restrains his mouth.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:142: However, the trait of Hillel the Elder surpasses all of these, for he was never particular about anything, and not even a stirring of anger was aroused in him at all (Shabbat 31a). This is certainly the one who is entirely clean of anger.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:143: And behold, our Sages, of blessed memory, warned us (Shabbat 34a) that even for a matter of a commandment one should not become angry — even a teacher toward his student, and a father toward his son — not that he should not discipline them, but he should discipline them without anger, only in order to guide them on the straight path; and the anger he displays to them should be an anger of the face, not an anger of the heart. And Solomon said (Ecclesiastes 7:9): "Be not hasty in your spirit to be angry, etc." And it says (Job 5:2): "for anger kills the foolish man." And they said, of blessed memory (Eruvin 65b): a person is recognized by three things: by his cup, by his purse, and by his anger.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:144: Envy, too, is nothing but a lack of understanding and folly, for the envious person gains nothing for himself and causes no loss to the one he envies, but only harms himself, as Scripture says, which I have already cited (Job 5:2): "and envy slays the simple."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:145: And indeed, there is one whose folly is so great that if he sees some good come to his fellow, he breaks down within himself and worries and grieves until even the good things in his own possession no longer give him pleasure, because of the grief he feels at what he sees in his fellow's hand; and of him the wise man said (Proverbs 14:30): "envy is rottenness of the bones."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:146: However, there are others who do not grieve and suffer so much, yet still feel some pain within themselves, or at least their spirit is cooled upon seeing another attain some additional level of rank — if it is not one of his closest friends, all the more so if it is one to whom he has no great affection, all the more so if he is a stranger from another land.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:147: And you will see that with their mouths they may speak as though rejoicing or giving thanks over his good fortune, but their heart is faint within them. This is something that happens generally to most people, for even though they are not truly envious persons, they have nevertheless not become entirely clean of it — all the more so if the fellow succeeds in his own profession, for "every craftsman hates his fellow craftsman" (Bereishit Rabbah 19), and all the more so if he succeeds in it more than he.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:148: And indeed, if they knew and understood that no person touches what is prepared for his fellow even by a hairsbreadth (Yoma 38b), and that everything, for everyone, comes from the Lord according to His wondrous counsel and unknowable wisdom, they would have no reason at all to grieve over the good fortune of their fellows.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:149: This is what the prophet foretold to us concerning the future time, that in order for the good fortune of Israel to be complete, the Holy One, blessed be He, will first remove from our hearts this unseemly trait, and then no one will grieve over another's good fortune, nor will the successful person need to conceal himself and his affairs because of envy.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:150: This is what is written (Isaiah 11:13): "And the envy of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off; Ephraim shall not envy Judah, etc." — this is the peace and tranquility of the ministering angels, all of whom rejoice in their service, each one in his own place, with none envying his fellow at all, for they all know the truth in its truth and delight in the good that is theirs and rejoice in their portion.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:151: And you will see that the sister of envy is covetousness and desire, which wearies a person's heart until the day of his death, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Kohelet Rabbah 1): "no man dies with even half his desires fulfilled."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:152: And indeed, the essence of desire turns toward two main objects: the one is money, and the other is honor; both together are very evil and cause a person many evils.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:153: Behold, the desire for money is what binds him in the imprisonment of the world and places the cords of toil and business upon his arms, as in the verse (Ecclesiastes 5:9): "He who loves money shall never be satisfied with money."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:154: It is what removes him from his service, for how many prayers are lost, and how many commandments forgotten, because of excessive business dealing and the toil of commerce — all the more so Torah study! And they have already said, of blessed memory (Eruvin 55a): "it is not across the sea" (Deuteronomy 30:13) — referring to those who cross the sea for trade.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:155: And so we learned (Avot 2:6): not all who increase in business grow wise thereby. It is what delivers him to many dangers and saps his strength through excessive worry, even after he has acquired much. And so we learned (ibid.): whoever increases possessions increases worry. It is what causes him, many times, to transgress the commandments of the Torah and even the statutes of natural reason.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:156: Greater still than this is the desire for honor, for a person could conceivably conquer his inclination regarding money and other pleasures, but honor is what presses upon him hardest, for he cannot bear or endure seeing himself lower than his fellows. Because of this, many have stumbled and been lost.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:157: Behold, Jeroboam the son of Nevat was banished from the World to Come only because of honor, as they said, of blessed memory (Sanhedrin 102a): the Holy One, blessed be He, seized him by his garment and said to him: Repent, and I, you, and the son of Jesse shall stroll together in the Garden of Eden. He said to Him: Who will be at the head? He said to him: The son of Jesse will be at the head. He said: If so, I do not want it.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:158: What caused Korach to be destroyed, he and his entire assembly with him? Only honor, and Scripture says explicitly (Numbers 16:10): "and you seek the priesthood also." And the Sages, of blessed memory (Bamidbar Rabbah 18), told us that all this followed from his seeing Elitzafan the son of Uzziel made a prince, when he himself had wanted to be made prince in his place.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:159: This, according to the opinion of our Sages, of blessed memory, is what caused the spies to bring forth a slanderous report about the Land, causing death to themselves and to their entire generation, out of their fear that their honor would diminish upon entering the Land — that they would no longer be princes of Israel, and others would arise in their place.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:160: Why did Saul begin to lie in wait for David? Only because of honor, as it is said (I Samuel 18:7): "and the women, singing as they played, answered, Saul has slain, etc.; and Saul eyed David from that day forward."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:161: What caused Joab to put Amasa to death? Only honor, since David had said to him (II Samuel 19:14): "may you be commander of the army before me continually" — in place of Joab, provoking his jealousy.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:162: In sum: honor presses upon a person's heart more than any other longing or desire in the world. And if not for this, a person would already be content to eat whatever he could, to wear whatever would cover his nakedness, and to dwell in a house that would shelter him from mishaps, and his livelihood would be easy for him, and he would not need to labor to grow rich at all.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:163: But so as not to see himself lowly and inferior to his fellows, he immerses himself in the thickness of this beam, and there is no end to all his toil. Therefore our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot 4:21): envy, desire, and honor drive a person out of the world. And they warned us (ibid. 6:5): do not seek greatness, and do not covet honor.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:164: How many there are who afflict themselves with hunger and lower themselves to be supported by charity, rather than engage in a craft that they consider beneath their honor, for fear that their honor would thereby diminish. Is there any greater folly than this?
Mesillat Yesharim 11:165: And they would rather choose idleness — which leads to boredom, to lewdness, to theft, and to every kind of transgression — than lower their rank and demean their imagined honor.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:166: And indeed our Sages, of blessed memory, who guided and directed us always in the ways of truth, said (Avot 1:10): love work, and hate mastery over others. And they further said (Pesachim 113a): flay a carcass in the marketplace for pay, and do not say, I am a great man, I am a priest. And they further said (Bava Batra 110a): a person should always engage in work that is foreign to him rather than become dependent upon others.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:167: The general rule of the matter: honor is one of the greatest stumbling blocks that a person has. And it is impossible for him to be a faithful servant to his Maker so long as he is concerned for his own honor, for in any case his folly will lead him to detract from the honor of Heaven. This is what King David, peace be upon him, said (II Samuel 6:22): "and I will be yet more lightly esteemed than this, and will be lowly in my own eyes."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:168: And true honor is nothing other than genuine knowledge of the Torah. And so they said, of blessed memory (Avot 6:3): there is no honor except Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 3:35): "the wise shall inherit honor,"
Mesillat Yesharim 11:169: and apart from this, it is nothing but imagined and false honor — vanity, of no benefit whatsoever. And it is proper for one who wishes to be clean to become entirely purified and cleansed of it; then he will succeed.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:170: Now, I have included up to this point many of the particulars of cleanliness. And this is a paradigm case for all the other commandments and character traits as well. (Proverbs 1:5): "the wise man will hear and increase learning, and the man of understanding will acquire wise counsel."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:171: And behold, I cannot deny that there is some labor for a person to attain this cleanliness. Nevertheless, I say that it is not needed to the degree it appears at first glance, and that thinking about this matter is harder than actually doing it; for when a person sets it in his heart and firmly resolves to be among those who possess this good trait, then, with a small amount of practice, it will become far easier for him than he could have imagined. This is a matter that experience will confirm to be true.
Mesillat Yesharim 12:1:
The Ways of Acquiring Cleanliness
Now, the true means of acquiring cleanliness is constant reading in the words of the Sages, of blessed memory, whether in matters of halachah or in matters of ethical teaching.
Mesillat Yesharim 12:2: For once the obligation of cleanliness and its necessity have become clear to a person, and he has already attained watchfulness and alacrity in occupying himself with the ways of acquiring them and in distancing himself from what undermines them, no obstacles now remain for him in acquiring cleanliness except knowledge of the fine details of the commandments, so that he can be watchful in all of them.
